sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant that runs on your own computer and talks to you in the chat apps you already use, such as WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord and iMessage. It also has native apps for macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and Linux.
sixtySeconds.problem: Most AI assistants live in someone else's cloud and their own app. OpenClaw keeps state, memory and credentials on your hardware and brings the assistant into your existing chats, with the model (Claude, Codex or a local model) as a swappable plugin.
whoFor: People who want a private AI assistant on their own machine
Users who want to chat with an assistant over WhatsApp, Telegram or Slack
Teams that want a shared assistant on one Gateway
Developers who want to extend an assistant with skills and plugins
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want an assistant you host yourself that reaches you in many chat apps and lets you swap models. If you just want a chat window in the browser, a hosted assistant is simpler.
requirements: Node.js (the installer provides it if needed; npm installs need Node 24.16.0+ or 26.1.0+)
Access to a model provider (hosted or local)
Accounts for the chat apps you connect

overview: OpenClaw runs a local Gateway, the control plane for sessions, tools, events and chat connections. You talk to it through its Control UI, CLI or terminal UI, or through channels like WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Signal and iMessage. Companion apps add voice, camera, screen and device actions on supported platforms.

Models and agent harnesses are plugins, so you can switch between hosted providers and local models without changing anything else. The README says OpenClaw itself only phones home for a daily version check by default; your prompts go to the model provider and chat platforms you set up.
It is developed in the open by the OpenClaw Foundation, an independent non-profit. Tools, skills and plugins extend what the assistant can do, and ClawHub is where plugins are shared.

troubleshooting.problem: Unknown people can't message the assistant
troubleshooting.solution: Direct-message channels pair unknown senders by default. Approve them with openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code>.
That flag needs npm 11.16+ or 12. On older npm, leave it out.

troubleshooting.problem: Plain npm install fails when building from source
troubleshooting.solution: The repository is a pnpm workspace; use pnpm install, not npm install.
